Leave Quotation Rules at Paratext's defaults — learners correct them during Lesson 2. RUNDA is already on the Send/Receive server at this starting state; add the learner as described in Step 5 above. A prebuilt backup is available from Kevin, for a learner who can't use Send/Receive.

Expected results (Quotations check):

State All books Matthew What the learner should notice Paratext defaults (start of Exercise 2.2) 1110 — Mostly "Closing quote [ ’ U+2019 ] found as a word medial character…", plus "Second-level quote mark found without a preceding first-level quote: ‘" (e.g. Matthew 2:6, 4:4, 4:6) and "Closing quote [ ’ U+2019 ] found without matching opening…" (Matthew 5:10). Guillemets aren't in the defaults. Exercise 2.2 settings (First level « « », Second level ‘ none ’, Third level none, list p) 847 252 The Second-level-without-first results are gone. Almost all that remains is the word-medial ’ (Exercise 2.3's subject), plus the 5:3 "Opening quote mark found without matching closing quote mark: «".

The point to listen for when you review: 1110 → 847 looks like little progress, but almost all of the 847 are one apostrophe clash. The learner should be reading the messages, not the count.

docs.title: Project Setup: VELNA, MENDA, and Waku (Scenario bank)
docs.text:
Each scenario-bank project needs enough text to produce meaningful check results, but no deliberate errors need to be seeded — learners correct these projects from Paratext's defaults, independently, having never seen them before.

Project Quotation style Minimum books suggested VELNA Guillemet outer (« / »), curly single inner (‘ / ’) — Guillemet style (Scenario A). Include words with ’ (U+2019) as apostrophes so learners encounter the apostrophe conflict. Matthew, Luke, John (dialogue-heavy) MENDA Double guillemets outer, reversed single guillemets inner: «...›...‹...»; Third level returns to «...» — include at least one third-level quote (John 19:21) (Scenario B) John (dialogue-heavy, contains the 19:21 third-level example) Waku Em dash as both opener and closer: —...—, with em dash continuation mark; Second level “...”; Third level ‘...’ (Scenario C) Matthew, Mark, Luke, John, Acts (stretch exercise; Acts is required — the scenario's check steps use its extended multi-paragraph speeches; Mark 13 carries most of the parenthetical em dashes and John 17 the same-character ambiguity that the scenario's seven residual results depend on)

Apply the correct quotation characters for each language throughout the text. Leave Quotation Rules at Paratext's defaults — learners correct them as part of the scenario.

Expected results at the defaults, and after correction (Quotations check, all books):

Project At Paratext's defaults After the scenario's configuration Note for review VELNA 264 — mostly "Second-level quote mark found without a preceding first-level quote: ‘", plus word-medial ’ (e.g. Matthew 1:1) 3: word-medial ’ at Matthew 1:1, Luke 1:1 and John 1:1 The ’ apostrophe results remain after correction (expected; see Scenario A). 264 → 3. MENDA "No errors found." "No errors found." At the defaults this is a false clean result. Menda's text does use guillemets (confirmed in the Punctuation inventory), but none of them are in the defaults, so the check recognizes no quote marks at all. Ask the learner why that isn't good news. Because the configured run gives the same message, the result alone can't tell you the learner configured Menda: look at their Quote marks tab. Waku "No errors found." 7 (Scenario C's residuals, including John 17:26 "Closing quote mark is possibly missing before verse 18.1: —") If the learner changed only the marks and left the Second and Third level continuers filled in (as the defaults have them) and the list p p/q1 b/q1, they get an 8th result: Matthew 13:14 "Second-level quote mark found without a preceding first-level quote: “". Eight instead of seven means the defaults weren't fully corrected.

Reviewing Scenario B (MENDA). Menda holds only John, so a run on John and a run on all books are the same run. Verified in Paratext 9.5:

  • Full configuration. First level « none », Second level › none ‹, Third level « none », with the Quotation types check enabled at Use recommended settings: "No errors found." The result is the same whether the Continuer required at list is p p/q1 b/q1 or empty: once all three continuers are none, clearing the list changes nothing in the check. The scenario still has learners clear it, because Menda's conventions have no continuers and the course teaches setting what the conventions say. Check the list on their Quote marks tab.
  • The John 19:21 discovery prompt. Menda's Third level uses « and », the same characters as First level. With First and Second level correct but Third level left at the defaults (“ “ ”), the check gives exactly 4 results, all at John 19:21, and the same 4 whether the Third level continuer is “ or none:
  • "Opening quote mark found without matching closing quote mark: «"
  • "Opening quote mark found without matching closing quote mark: ›"
  • "Closing quote [ ‹ U+2039 ] found without matching opening. Caused by a missing opening quote, a missing continuer, or incorrectly defined continuer rules: ‹"
  • "Closing quote [ » U+00BB ] found without matching opening. Caused by a missing opening quote, a missing continuer, or incorrectly defined continuer rules: »"

The diagnostic to listen for: results only at 19:21 mean Third level wasn't changed; results throughout John point to First or Second level. - Second level reversed (‹ in Opening, › in Closing): 125 results throughout John, in pairs per verse: "Closing quote [ › U+203A ] found without matching opening. Caused by a missing opening quote, a missing continuer, or incorrectly defined continuer rules: ›" and "Opening quote mark found without matching closing quote mark: ‹". - « typed instead of » in the First and Third level Closing cells: 224 results in John, nearly all naming « ("Closing quote mark is possibly missing in this verse: «", "Opening quote mark found without matching closing quote mark: «"). The Example box on the Quote marks tab gives it away: it shows « where the closing mark should be (for example "upstairs.«"). Send the learner to the Example box. - OK is disabled, with a red ! beside Continuer required at. The tooltip reads "Cannot be blank if any Quote Continuer is specified." The learner cleared the list while a continuer was still set. Set all three continuers to none first, then clear the list.

All three scenario-bank projects are already on the Send/Receive server at their starting state; add the learner as described in Step 5 under the TAMBA setup. Prebuilt backups are available from Kevin, for a learner who can't use Send/Receive. The tables above are reference for anyone rebuilding a project from scratch, not a required setup step. If you do rebuild one: put Quotation Rules back to Paratext's defaults (see Overview) before backing up — or create the project fresh in Paratext 9.5, which saves the defaults on creation. Learners must start from the defaults, not from the verified configuration. VELNA is new as of this revision (it replaces RUNDA's prior role in Scenario A, so the two must be distinct projects — do not reuse the RUNDA backup for VELNA).

docs.title: Lesson 4 Seeding
docs.text:
The five underlying issues in Exercise 4.1 must be manually introduced into the Phase B TAMBAB project text. Seed each error as follows. Note that seed #3 produces three separate check results (at 3:10, 3:16, and 3:21) from one broken mark — confirmed in a Paratext 9.5 run — so the project will show seven total results from these five seeds, not five.

# Location What to do in the text 1 Matthew 5:12, 7:27 Delete the closing ” (U+201D) in 5:12 and the closing ” (U+201D) in 7:27 — leave every opening “ (U+201C) in place, including the continuers and the “ that reopens the speech at the start of 5:13. With both closing marks gone, Jesus's speech that opens at 5:3 is never closed, which creates an unclosed-quote result reported back at Matthew 5:3. In practice the check reports this as "Closing quote mark is possibly missing before verse [X]," where [X] is wherever the next real closing mark in the project happens to fall — confirmed in a Paratext 9.5 run to trace all the way to 7:28. 2 Luke 4:18 Insert a stray “ (U+201C) immediately before the first word of the Isaiah citation. Tamba does not mark narrator scripture citations; the stray mark mimics a translator adding a dialogue opener by mistake. 3 John 3:16 Verse 3:16 begins a new \p paragraph inside Jesus's speech to Nicodemus, so in Phase A it opens with the First level Quote Continuer “ (U+201C). Replace that “ at the start of 3:16 with a straight " (U+0022). This one corrupted character breaks quotation tracking on both sides of it: confirmed in a Paratext 9.5 run to produce three linked results — "Quote opened; see following message for error" at 3:10 (the quotation's true start), "Expected continuers [“] are missing OR quote not closed; see preceding message" at 3:16 (the corrupted mark itself), and "Closing quote [” U+201D] found without matching opening" at 3:21 (the orphaned close). Replacing the " at the start of 3:16 with “ (U+201C) and re-running clears all three (verified in Paratext 9.5; replacing it with ‘ is not the fix). 4 Acts 2:28 Delete the closing ’ (U+2019) in 2:28 that ends Peter's Psalm 16 citation; leave the opening ‘ (U+2018) in 2:25 in place. In Phase A the citation is one Second level span across several paragraph breaks, with no close/reopen at the breaks, and it passes the check clean — Tamba's Second level has no continuer, so the span is valid. Removing only the close leaves the citation unclosed, reported at Acts 2:25; learners identify it as a real error and restore the ’ in 2:28. 5 Romans 1:1 In a possessive or contraction in the verse text (e.g., God’s word), use ’ (U+2019) as the apostrophe. Phase A text has no apostrophes; this one creates the conflict between the Second level closing mark (U+2019) and a word-medial apostrophe, generating a spurious quotation result. Confirmed on a real Paratext 9.5 build: this result is permanent — adding ’ to Word-medial punctuation does not clear it. Do not seed this expecting learners to reach zero results in Romans; Exercise 4.2's completion criteria account for this one exception.

After seeding, run the Quotation check and confirm all seven results (five seeds, with #3 producing three) appear before distributing the project to learners. The Exercise 4.1 table already reflects verified Paratext 9.5 message wording for this build; if you rebuild the project from scratch and the wording or locations differ, update that table to match before distributing the course.

docs.title: General Facilitation Notes
docs.text:
• Discovery-first ordering: Each lesson shows the answer key after the discovery prompts, not before. Encourage learners to write down their prediction before scrolling to the expected configuration.
  • Scenario C (Waku): The em-dash scenario is the hardest. It is appropriate as a stretch exercise or for learners who have completed Lessons 1–4 confidently and want a challenge.

docs.title: Assessment Quiz — Configuring Quotation Rules in Paratext
Assessment quiz (20 questions)
docs.text: This quiz covers all five lessons of the course, including the scenario bank. You need 80% (16/20) to pass. Questions are a mix of recall, scenario-based application, and true/false. Everything asked here is drawn directly from the lessons — work them first.

docs.title: Section 1: What the Quotation Check Does (Questions 1-3)
docs.text:
Question 1: Which two inputs must be configured before the Quotations check can produce trustworthy results? - A) Language Settings and its Other Characters tab - B) The book scope and the Quotations tick box in Run basic checks - C) The Quote marks tab and the Quotation types tab - D) The Example preview and the Copy quote mark settings button

Question 2: TAMBA is still at Paratext's default Quotation Rules. The Quotations check on all books reports five results in John 17, each "Opening quote mark found without matching closing quote mark: “". The team lead asks whether they should add the closing marks. What do you tell them? - A) Yes; five unclosed speeches in one chapter are real errors in the text - B) Not yet; these are still Paratext's settings, so correct those first - C) Yes, but only after the Quotation types check has been enabled too - D) No; delete the five opening marks instead, so no speech is left open

Question 3: True or False: On a project still at Paratext's default Quotation Rules, the Quotations check can report a handful of plausible results, a flood of results, or "No errors found", and none of these can be trusted until the settings match the team's conventions. - A) True - B) False

docs.title: Section 2: Setting Up Quote Marks (Questions 4-8)
docs.text:
Question 4: Runda's conventions have no Third level, but its Quote marks tab still holds Paratext's defaults at Third level (“ “ ”). What do you do with the Third level cells? - A) Leave the defaults; an unused level produces no results - B) Change them to « « », so they match Runda's First level - C) Change them to ‘ ‘ ’, so they match Runda's Second level - D) Set all three Third level cells, Continuer included, to none

Question 5: Correcting TAMBA's defaults, you start by adding pi/pi to the Continuer required at field, click OK and run the Quotations check on all books. The five John 17 results are gone and the check reports "No errors found". Nothing else on the Quote marks tab has been changed yet. What do you do? - A) Set the Second and Third level continuers to none; the clean run shows the list is complete - B) Complete the list to Tamba's six entries; the default continuer cells cause no results in its text - C) Set every level's continuer to none, then type Tamba's full six-entry list into the field - D) Set the Second and Third level continuers to none, then type Tamba's six-entry list

Question 6: On the Quote marks tab you have changed every cell that differed from the team's conventions. Before clicking OK, what is the recommended way to confirm you picked the right characters? - A) Check the sample text in the Example section at the bottom of the dialog - B) Hover each column label and read the character named in the status bar - C) Compare the shapes in the grid with the marks in the convention table - D) Click OK, then run the check on the whole NT and compare the counts

Question 7: On RUNDA you correct the First level cells to « « » but leave the Continuer required at list at the default p p/q1 b/q1. The check on Matthew reports "Expected continuers [«] are missing" at Matthew 2:6 and 4:6, both poetry quoted inside speech. What does this point to, and what is the fix? - A) The list is too long: replace it with just p, then run the check again - B) The list is too short: add q1 as well, then run the check again - C) The continuer cell is at fault: clear First level's continuer, then run again - D) The text is missing continuers: add « before both poems, then run again

Question 8: Runda uses ’ (U+2019) as its Second level closing mark and also as an apostrophe inside words such as don’t, and the check flags those apostrophes as word-medial closing quotes. You add ’ to ☰ > Project settings > Language Settings > Other Characters > Word-medial punctuation, click OK, close the results panel and run the check again. What happens? - A) The word-medial apostrophe results are gone from the new run - B) Paratext won't save the setting, because ’ is already a quote mark - C) Every word-medial apostrophe result is still reported, as before - D) Those results clear, but every Second level ’ is now flagged instead

docs.title: Section 3: Configuring Quotation Types (Questions 9-11)
docs.text:
Question 9: Tamba repeats its First level opening mark “ (U+201C) at the head of each paragraph when a speech runs on. The recommended setting for Continued quotation is Never use quote marks. With the Quotation types check enabled, what should you do? - A) Leave it; Continued quotation applies only to Second and Third level speech - B) Choose Custom settings and set Continued quotation to Use quote marks - C) Leave it, and clear the First level continuer cell on the Quote marks tab - D) Leave it; the continuer cell on the Quote marks tab overrides this setting

Question 10: The Tamba team tells you that when the narrator reports what someone said ("He told them that the harvest was near"), they write it as plain narrative text, and that is how every such verse should stay. The recommended setting for Indirect is Quote marks are optional. What do you do? - A) Leave Indirect at Optional; with no marks in the text, there is nothing for it to flag - B) Choose Custom settings and set Indirect to Use quote marks, so each verse is checked - C) Leave Indirect at Optional, which flags any mark a translator adds to reported speech - D) Choose Custom settings and set Indirect to Never use quote marks

Question 11: You have switched Tamba's Quotation types tab to Custom settings to change three types. The team confirms that a self-quote must be marked just like any other direct speech. Self quote currently shows Use quote marks. What do you do with it? - A) Change it to Quote marks are optional, the safer choice on a custom tab - B) Change it to Never use quote marks, since Normal already checks direct speech - C) Leave it at Use quote marks, and go on to the three types that need changing - D) Change it to Quote marks are optional and note each self-quote for the consultant

docs.title: Section 4: Interpreting and Clearing the Check (Questions 12-17)
docs.text:
Question 12: TAMBAB is configured with the Lesson 2–3 settings, including Quotation from another source = Quote marks are optional. The check reports at Luke 4:18: "Closing quote mark is possibly missing before verse 20". Tamba does not mark narrator scripture citations, and you find a “ (U+201C) immediately before the Isaiah citation in 4:18. How do you classify and handle this result? - A) Real error: add a closing ” (U+201D) before verse 20, where the check points - B) Real error: delete the stray “ (U+201C) before the citation in 4:18 - C) Configuration problem: set Quotation from another source to Use quote marks - D) Neither: leave the result and document it with a Project Note at 4:18

Question 13: In TAMBAB, three results appear together. John 3:10: "Quote opened; see following message for error". John 3:16: "Expected continuers [“] are missing OR quote not closed; see preceding message". John 3:21: "Closing quote [” U+201D] found without matching opening. Caused by a missing opening quote, a missing continuer, or incorrectly defined continuer rules". Verse 3:16 starts a new \p paragraph inside Jesus's speech and begins with a straight " (U+0022). What do you do? - A) Replace the " at 3:16 with ‘ (U+2018), close the results panel and run the check again - B) Add " (U+0022) as the First level continuer on the Quote marks tab, then run the check again - C) Replace the " at 3:16 with “ (U+201C), and add an opening “ before the ” at 3:21 - D) Replace the " at 3:16 with “ (U+201C), close the results panel and run the check again

Question 14: You have fixed every real error the check found in Matthew, but six results remain. All six read "Opening quote mark found without matching closing quote mark: “", each at a different verse, and the translation team confirms the marks in those verses are written the way they intend. What is your next step? - A) Treat them as a configuration problem: find and adjust the setting - B) Classify them as Neither: leave all six and add a Project Note to each - C) Remove the flagged marks from those verses so that Matthew reaches zero - D) Leave Matthew as it is and expand the scope to the rest of the NT

Question 15: You start Exercise 4.2 in TAMBAB, working the result list toward zero actionable errors. How do you scope the check? - A) Run all NT books at once, so no result is missed before you start fixing - B) Start with Romans, so the known exception is dealt with first - C) Run Matthew alone until it is clean, then add one book at a time - D) Start with whichever book shows the most results in a full NT run

Question 16: In TAMBAB, you add the two missing ” (U+201D) marks at Matthew 5:12 and 7:27, then click Rerun on the results panel that is still open. The Matthew 5:3 result "Closing quote mark is possibly missing before verse 7:28" is still listed. What do you do next? - A) Undo the two edits, since the result shows they did not fix the problem - B) Keep looking for another missing ” between Matthew 5:3 and 7:28 - C) Close the results panel and run the check again from Run basic checks - D) Check the Continuer required at list, since the text is now correct

Question 17: Expanding TAMBAB book by book, every book now shows 0 results except Romans, which shows one, at 1:1: "Closing quote [’ U+2019] found as a word medial character. Sometimes caused when a closing quote is incorrectly used as an apostrophe". The verse has no dialogue, and the flagged ’ sits between two letters of a word. When is Romans finished? - A) Once adding ’ to Word-medial punctuation has cleared the result - B) Once the ’ is verified as an apostrophe and the result documented - C) Once the ’ is taken out of the word so that Romans shows 0 results - D) Once the translation team has rewritten 1:1 without the apostrophe

docs.title: Section 5: Applying the Workflow to Unfamiliar Languages (Questions 18-20)
docs.text:
Question 18: In the Menda project, Second level opens with › (U+203A) and closes with ‹ (U+2039). You accidentally enter ‹ in the Second level Opening cell and › in the Closing cell, then run the check on John. What do you see, and what is the fix? - A) No results; Paratext pairs single guillemets whichever way they point - B) Results only at John 19:21, where Third level reuses « and » - C) Second level results throughout; edit the text so ‹ opens and › closes - D) Second level results throughout; swap the two cells, check the Example

Question 19: Waku uses an em dash — (U+2014) as its First level opening, continuer and closing mark. With Waku correctly configured, the check still reports six "found as a word medial character" results on em dashes that the translation team confirms are parenthetical asides, not speech. What is the right handling? - A) Add a Project Note at each verse, and raise other punctuation for asides with the team - B) Add — (U+2014) to Word-medial punctuation so those dashes are read as part of words - C) Replace the parenthetical em dashes with brackets yourself so the count reaches zero - D) Set every quotation type to Quote marks are optional so the dashes are no longer flagged

Question 20: True or False: Once a project's Quote marks and Quotation types tabs correctly describe the language, the Quotations check run on every book will return zero results. - A) True - B) False

docs.title: Answer key
docs.text:
1. C | 2. B | 3. A | 4. D | 5. D | 6. A | 7. A | 8. C | 9. B | 10. D | 11. C | 12. B | 13. D | 14. A | 15. C | 16. C | 17. B | 18. D | 19. A | 20. B

Rationales

  1. C — Lesson 1: the check reads the Quote marks tab (which characters are quote marks, and at what level) and the Quotation types tab (whether each kind of speech requires, forbids or optionally allows marks), and both must be set to match the team's conventions. Language Settings, the Run basic checks options and the Example/Copy controls are not those two inputs.
  2. B — Lesson 1 Exercise 1.1: the five John 17 results come from Paratext's default settings, not from the text, which the course has checked and found correct. Correct the settings first and run the check again; anything that still points at the text then goes back to the translation team. Adding or deleting marks to clear a default-settings result changes correct Scripture to satisfy a setting nobody chose, and enabling the Quotation types check does not change that.
  3. A (True) — Lesson 1 Content: at the defaults the check can show a handful of plausible results (Tamba's five in John 17), a flood (Runda's 1110) or a false silence (Menda's "No errors found" on a text full of dialogue, because none of its marks are in the defaults). The defaults are Paratext's, not the team's, so none of these results can be trusted yet.
  4. D — Lesson 2 Exercise 2.2 and the scenario workflow: the grid is never empty, so correcting it means changing every cell that differs from the conventions, including unused levels that must be set to none. A cell you leave at the default is still Paratext's choice, not the team's: in Runda's current text the Third level defaults happen to add no results (A's reason is true), but as with Q5 a clean check does not prove the settings are right. Runda's First and Second level marks are not its Third level, because Runda has none.
  5. D — Lesson 2 Exercise 2.1: pi/pi alone clears the John 17 results, and the default Second and Third level continuers produce no results in Tamba's text, so "No errors found" does not prove the settings are right. The check only reports what the current text happens to trip over. Tamba's conventions have no Second or Third level continuer and a six-entry Continuer required at list (p p/q1 m/q1 s1/pi pi/pi b/q1, against the default's three plus your pi/pi), so set both. Stopping after either half because the run is clean leaves a default the team never chose; and Tamba's First level does repeat “ as its continuer, so that cell stays as it is rather than going to none.
  6. A — Lesson 2: confirm the characters in the Example section at the bottom of the dialog before clicking OK. Hovering a label shows a description of the field, not the character in the cell; similar-looking marks can be different code points, so comparing shapes is not enough; and a check run is not a substitute for verifying what you entered.
  7. A — Lesson 2 Exercise 2.2 and its table: "Expected continuers [«] are missing" at each place a listed marker occurs inside speech means the list is too long; the default p/q1 names a marker Runda's text does not continue at. Runda's text carries « only at \p, so its list is p alone. The fix is in the field, not the text: the text is the authority and the list is your description of it. A too-short list shows a different symptom (unclosed-quote results inside a long speech), and clearing the continuer cell would break Runda's real continuers.
  8. C — Lesson 2 Exercise 2.3: Word-medial punctuation does not suppress the result once the character is also a configured quote mark, so every genuine apostrophe is still flagged on a fresh run. Paratext warns that unique characters are recommended, but it saves the setting. Treat each result as an expected false positive; the lasting fix is a different, unique apostrophe character, which is an orthography decision for the translation team to make, not you.
  9. B — Lesson 3 Exercise 3.2: with a First level continuer, a mark is expected at the head of each continued paragraph, so "Never use quote marks" would flag every expected continuer as an error. Switch to Custom settings and set Continued quotation to Use quote marks. The setting concerns Tamba's First level continuer, the Quote marks tab does not override it, and clearing the continuer cell would break the Quotations check configured in Lesson 2.
  10. D — Lesson 3 Exercise 3.2: Tamba never marks reported speech, and Optional does not flag errors for its type, so it would never catch a stray mark a translator adds there (the claim that it does is false, and "nothing to flag" misses that the setting's job is to catch marks that shouldn't be there). Switch to Custom settings and set Indirect to Never use quote marks so a stray mark gets caught. Use quote marks would flag every correctly unmarked verse.
  11. C — Lesson 3 Exercise 3.2: Self quote already defaults to Use quote marks, which is what Tamba needs, so it stays as it is while you change the other three types. Optional would stop the check flagging a self-quote whose marks are missing, and Never would flag correctly marked ones. Not every recommended default is wrong; check each type against the language's conventions rather than changing all seven.
  12. B — Lesson 4 Exercise 4.1 item 2: the “ before the Isaiah citation is a stray mark, like a translator adding a dialogue opener by mistake, so it is a real error: delete it (on a live project, confirm with the translation team that it doesn't belong, as Lesson 4's self-assessment 3 does). The check treats the stray mark as a legitimate new opening and reports its close as missing wherever the next real closing mark falls, so adding a ” where it points chases the symptom, not the cause. Optional is the correct Quotation from another source setting for Tamba, and a real error is fixed, not documented.
  13. D — Lesson 4 Exercise 4.1 item 3: 3:16 starts a new \p paragraph inside Jesus's First level speech, so it should open with Tamba's First level Quote Continuer “ (U+201C). That one wrong character produces all three results; replace it, close the results panel and run the check again (not Rerun on the open panel), and all three clear together. ‘ is the Second level opening mark, not the continuer; the Quote marks tab describes the language's convention, not a stray character; and there is nothing to fix at 3:10 or 3:21.
  14. A — Lesson 4 Content, Exercise 4.2 and self-assessment 2: the same message repeated across many verses usually points to a configuration gap, and once the team has confirmed the text the remaining results are about the settings. Find the rule or setting (for an unclosed-quote message like this one, Lesson 2 points to a Continuer required at list that is too short), adjust it, then close the results panel and run the check again. Editing text to quiet the check is never right; Neither is reserved for the quote-mark/apostrophe collision, which this message is not; and you expand the scope only once Matthew is clean.
  15. C — Lesson 4 Exercise 4.2 steps 1 and 5: limit the scope to Matthew and work it to zero results, then expand one book at a time through the NT. A full-NT result list is overwhelming while a single-book list is actionable, and Matthew has no unresolvable cases, so a true zero is the right target there.
  16. C — Lesson 4 Exercise 4.2 note: clicking Rerun on the panel that is already open does not pick up your text changes; it keeps showing the old results, so a correct fix looks as if it failed. Close the results panel and run the check again from ☰ > Tools > Run basic checks... before deciding anything about your edits.
  17. B — Lesson 4 Exercise 4.2 step 5 and completion criteria: Romans is expected to stop at 1 result, the 1:1 apostrophe, which is neither a real error nor a configuration problem. Adding ’ to Word-medial punctuation does not clear it (Lesson 2 Exercise 2.3, Lesson 4 Exercise 4.1 item 5), and the apostrophe is correct as written, so there is no text edit. Verify it, document it, and Romans is done. Raising a unique apostrophe character with the translation team is worthwhile, but it is their orthography decision and Romans does not wait on it.
  18. D — Scenario B (Menda): with the Second level cells reversed, the check reports results in pairs throughout John, "Closing quote [ › U+203A ] found without matching opening…" and "Opening quote mark found without matching closing quote mark: ‹". Swap the cells so › opens and ‹ closes, confirm in the Example section, and with Third level also set to Menda's « none » the check reports "No errors found". Paratext does not pair single guillemets whichever way they point, and the text follows Menda's convention, so it is the configuration that changes, not the text; results only at John 19:21 come from Third level cells left at the defaults, not from reversed Second level cells.
  19. A — Scenario C (Waku): Paratext cannot tell an em dash used for speech from one used for an aside, and the scenario confirms a correct configuration still ends with these results, so no setting clears them. Add a Project Note (☰ > Insert > Project note...) at each verse the result is reported at, so the consultant can verify it during review. Whether to use different punctuation for asides is the translation team's call: raise it with them rather than editing the text yourself.
  20. B (False) — Scenario bank summary and Lesson 4 Exercise 4.2: a correct configuration can still leave results that need human review, such as Waku's seven residual results or the Romans 1:1 apostrophe in Tamba. The target is zero actionable errors, which is not always a zero-length results list.

docs.title: Video script
docs.text:
Companion recording script for the course Configuring Quotation Rules in Paratext. This is an orientation/overview video: a screen-capture walkthrough that shows learners the shape of the tool and the workflow before they sit down and do the hands-on lessons. It is not a full read-aloud of the lessons — the detailed, click-by-click exercise work happens in the numbered lesson files, where learners can pause and work at their own pace. The recording happens outside this repo; hosting the video externally and linking it from the course in Moodle is a separate human step.

Estimated runtime: 13-15 minutes (overview companion to a multi-hour hands-on course). Companion lesson file(s): 01-what-the-quotation-check-does.md through 05-scenario-bank.md — one orientation segment per lesson.

docs.title: Overview / cold open
docs.text:
Runtime target: ~60-90 seconds. Open on a live screen recording, not a title slide.

On-screen: Screen recording of the TAMBA project, freshly received and untouched, so its Quotation Rules are still Paratext 9.5's defaults. The Run basic checks dialog is open with Quotations ticked (and nothing else) and Choose Books set to all NT books in the project. The presenter clicks OK, and the results panel lists five results, all in John 17 — at 17:1, 17:6, 17:13, 17:20 and 17:24 — each reading "Opening quote mark found without matching closing quote mark: “". Hold on the list long enough for all five to register. Do not open the verses. (This is the state captured in assets/ss-01-run-basic-checks.png and assets/ss-01-default-results.png — record it live.) Optional lower-third over the list: Text: correct. Settings: Paratext's defaults.

Voiceover: "Here's a message you'll get on a real project. The team lead says the quotation check found five places in John 17 where they forgot to close a speech, and asks whether they should add the closing marks. This is what they're looking at: five results, all in John 17, each one saying a speech was opened and never closed. They look like five real mistakes, but they aren't. The text is correct. What's wrong is the settings. This project still has the Quotation Rules Paratext gives every new project. Nobody on the team chose them, and they don't describe how this team writes. If the team adds five closing marks, they've changed correct Scripture to satisfy settings nobody chose. Over the next few minutes I'll show you the two settings that turn this check into a list you can trust. Then you'll set them up yourself."

docs.title: Segment 1 — Why a check on the defaults can't be trusted yet (companion to Lesson 1)
docs.text:
~2 minutes. Concept framing. Keep it fast — this is the "why," the lesson carries the "how."

On-screen Voiceover / talking points Reopen the Run basic checks dialog (it closed when OK was clicked in the cold open). Hover over the yellow information bar at the bottom of the dialog so its text is legible on screen. "See this yellow bar? It says the accuracy of the check depends on the information you've given it. That's the whole story. The check is only as good as the settings it's reading." Cancel the dialog. Open ☰ > Project settings > Quotation Rules, Quote marks tab, on TAMBA without changing anything: “ “ ” at First level, ‘ ‘ ’ at Second level, “ “ ” at Third level, and Continuer required at reading p p/q1 b/q1. (State shown in assets/ss-02-quote-marks-tab-defaults.png.) Click Cancel. "And here's the trap. This tab isn't empty. Every new project in Paratext 9.5 starts with these marks: curly double quotes, curly single quotes inside them, and a default list down here. So the check runs and reports results, and everything looks set up. But Paratext chose these settings, not the translation team. Until someone compares every cell with the team's own conventions, the check is measuring their text against somebody else's rules." Cut to a simple two-box slide: 1. Quote marks tab — which characters are quote marks, and at what level. 2. Quotation types tab — when marks are expected. "The check reads two inputs. Input one: which characters in your text actually are quotation marks, and at which nesting level. Input two: for each kind of speech, whether marks should be there, should never be there, or don't matter. Both have to describe the team's conventions before the check's results mean anything." Three-line slide: A few plausible results — TAMBA: 5 / A flood — RUNDA: 1110 / A false silence — MENDA: "No errors found". On the second line, cut briefly to the RUNDA results panel at the defaults showing the 1110 count (assets/ss-02-runda-default-results.png); on the third, cut briefly to a live run on MENDA at the defaults returning "No errors found". Return to the slide. "Defaults mislead you in one of three ways. You get a few plausible results, like the five you just saw. Or you get a flood: Runda, which you'll meet in Lesson 2, reports more than a thousand. Or you get a false silence: Menda's text is full of dialogue, but none of its marks are in the defaults, so the check doesn't recognize anything as a quote mark and says 'No errors found'. That isn't a clean bill of health. It means the check isn't recognizing anything. Five results, a thousand, or none, you can't trust any of them until the settings match the team's conventions. Once they do, anything that still points at the text goes back to the translation team as a question. Changing the text is their call, not yours."

docs.title: Segment 2 — The Quote marks tab (companion to Lesson 2)
docs.text:
~3.5 minutes. The heart of the video. Show the navigation and the grid; do NOT walk every cell for every level — show the pattern once.

On-screen Voiceover / talking points Live navigation: click the project menu ☰ > Project settings > Quotation Rules. (State shown in assets/ss-02-project-menu-quotation-rules.png.) Land on the Quote marks tab, still showing the defaults. "Here's input one. Project menu, Project settings, Quotation Rules, and the Quote marks tab. This is where you tell Paratext the characters." Slow pan across the three-by-three grid, still at the defaults. Highlight the three rows, then the three columns. (Layout in assets/ss-02-quote-marks-tab-defaults.png.) "Three rows are your nesting levels: first-level speech, a quote inside a quote, and a quote inside that. Three columns: the Opening mark, the Quote Continuer at a new paragraph, and the Closing mark. The middle column answers one question: when a speech runs across paragraphs, does this language repeat a mark at the head of each new paragraph? Your job here isn't to fill in a blank grid. You compare every cell with the team's conventions and change the ones that don't match. For Tamba, the whole first level already matches. Tamba repeats its opening mark at each new paragraph, and so does the default. But Tamba repeats nothing at the second and third levels, and the defaults do, so those two continuer cells have to change." Click the dropdown arrow (▼) on the Second level Quote Continuer at new paragraph cell so the list appears, and select none. Repeat for Third level. Then show the Example preview at the bottom reading “…‘…’…”. "Always choose characters from the dropdown on each cell, never by typing. That's how you know you picked U+201C and not a straight keyboard quote. Choosing none counts as a change too. A cell you didn't look at is still Paratext's choice, not the team's. Each time, glance down at the Example preview. If the sample sentence shows the marks you expect, you got it right. It's your best safety check." Click into the Continuer required at field and replace p p/q1 b/q1 with p p/q1 m/q1 s1/pi pi/pi b/q1. Click OK. "This small field matters far more than its size suggests. The continuer cell tells the check which character continues a speech. This list tells it where to expect that character, by naming the paragraph markers. You build the list by looking at where the project's text actually carries the continuer. Lesson 2 shows you how." Re-run the Quotations check on TAMBA, all NT books with Choose Books. The panel reads "No errors found". "Same project, same text, nothing typed into Scripture, and the five John 17 results are gone. One more thing, though: a clean check on its own doesn't prove the settings are right. The check can only report what the current text happens to trip over. Some of the changes you just made never produced a result at all, so the check would have gone quiet with them still wrong. Set what the team's conventions say, and don't stop just because the list is empty." Brief cut to the Runda Quote marks tab after correction, showing guillemets and a filled First level Continuer cell. (assets/ss-02-runda-quote-marks.png.) "Different language, same grid. Runda uses French guillemets, and like Tamba it repeats its opening mark at each new paragraph, so its continuer cell holds « instead of “. None of those characters were in the defaults, which is why Runda came back with more than a thousand results. The tab doesn't change from language to language. Only the characters do." Cut to Language Settings: ☰ > Project settings > Language Settings > Other Characters tab, with ’ in the Word-medial punctuation field, warning icon visible. (assets/ss-02-language-settings-other-chars.png.) "Here's a gotcha that traps almost everyone, and it doesn't play out the way you'd expect. If your closing single quote is U+2019, and the same character is also used as an apostrophe inside words, the check reads every apostrophe as a stray closing mark. This field, Word-medial punctuation under Language Settings, Other Characters, looks built for exactly this case. Add the character here, save, run a fresh check, and the apostrophes are still flagged. That's confirmed on Paratext 9.5: once a character is set as a quote mark, this setting doesn't override it. No setting fixes this one. The skill is recognizing it, confirming each one really is an apostrophe, and documenting it instead of hunting for a fix. A different apostrophe character would remove the collision, but that's an orthography decision for the translation team, not for you."

docs.title: Segment 3 — The Quotation types tab (companion to Lesson 3)
docs.text:
~2.5 minutes. Concept + the three custom changes. Don't recite all seven types on camera.

On-screen Voiceover / talking points Click the Quotation types tab. Show the seven type rows and the Recommended/Custom controls at the top. (assets/ss-03-quotation-types-tab.png.) "Input two is on the second tab. This one isn't about characters at all, it's about meaning. For each of seven kinds of speech, you tell Paratext to expect marks, never expect marks, or not care." Point to the Use recommended settings control, then to the enable checkbox at the top. "A new project starts on Use recommended settings, with the check itself switched off. For many projects the recommended settings are a fair baseline, but they're still Paratext's choice, so check them. Note the enable checkbox at the top: only a project administrator can tick it. You can configure everything else. If you're not an admin, set it up and then ask an admin to tick that box." Switch to Custom settings and change three rows — Quotation from another source to optional, Continued quotation to Use quote marks, and Indirect to Never use quote marks. Point out that Self quote is left alone because it already defaults to Use quote marks, which is what Tamba needs. "You only switch to Custom settings when the language does something different, and you check every row, because the defaults don't always match what you'd guess. In our Tamba project, three types need to change. Self quote turns out to be right already, so we leave it. That's the pattern: start from the recommended settings, and use custom settings for the differences the team has confirmed. Check against the real project, don't assume."

docs.title: Segment 4 — Reading and clearing results (companion to Lesson 4)
docs.text:
~2.5 minutes. Teach the mental model: real error vs. configuration problem. This is the payoff.

On-screen Voiceover / talking points Switch to TAMBAB, the Phase B copy of Tamba. Run the check across the whole New Testament. Show the short results panel with one result highlighted and the verse open alongside it. (assets/ss-04-results-with-highlight.png.) "For the last lesson you switch to a copy of Tamba that's already configured, with a few deliberate errors added to the text. Run the check and look at the difference. It's a short list now, and every result means something. This is a list you can actually work through." Slide: Real error → fix the text. / Configuration problem → fix the settings. "Every result is one of two things. A real error means the text really does have a missing, extra or wrong mark, and the verse gets corrected. On a live project, that correction goes through the translation team. A configuration problem means the check has exposed a gap in your settings. You fix the Quote marks tab or the types tab, and you do NOT edit correct text to make the warning go away." Screen: point to a message that repeats across many verses, versus a one-off message. "A quick tell: the same message on lots of verses usually means a configuration gap. A one-off usually means a real error in that one verse. Work from the top down, run the check fresh after each batch, and watch the count fall." Show the final results panel: one result left, the Romans 1:1 apostrophe. (assets/ss-04-final-results.png.) "The goal is zero results you still need to act on. Get Matthew clean first, then expand one book at a time. Zero doesn't mean the text is perfect. It means every result has been looked at and dealt with on purpose, and any that can't clear, like that apostrophe, are verified and documented. That's what a consultant is trusting when they pick up the book."

docs.title: Segment 5 — Applying it to any language (companion to the scenario bank)
docs.text:
~1.5 minutes. Motivate the scenario bank without solving it. Show one striking edge case.

On-screen Voiceover / talking points Cut to the Menda Quote marks tab after correction, Second level showing › opening and ‹ closing, with the Example preview confirming the nested order. (assets/ss-05-menda-quote-marks.png.) "Once you know the workflow, it's the same four steps for any language, however unusual its marks. Here's Menda, the project that said 'No errors found' at the defaults. Its second level opens with a right-pointing single guillemet and closes with a left-pointing one, the reverse of what your eye expects. Get them backwards and the check fires on every embedded quote. The Example preview at the bottom is how you catch that before you click OK." Slide listing the three scenario languages: Velna (guillemets), Menda (reversed nesting), Waku (em-dash — stretch). At "That last one won't fully clear by configuration alone," briefly cut to the Waku results panel showing seven remaining results on a correctly configured project (assets/ss-05-waku-residual-results.png), then return to the slide. "In the scenario bank you'll do three of these on your own. Each project starts on Paratext's defaults, so run the check first and see which kind of misleading result you get. Then compare, correct, check and triage. There's guillemets, that reversed nesting, and, if you want a stretch, a language that uses the em dash to both open and close. That last one won't fully clear through configuration alone. You'll document what's left in a Project Note so the consultant knows each result was reviewed on purpose, and you'll take the punctuation question to the translation team."

docs.title: Call to action / close
docs.text:
~45 seconds.

On-screen: Return to the clean, zero-results panel from Segment 4. End on a simple closing slide: Lessons 1-4 → Scenario Bank → submit to your mentor.

Voiceover: "That's the whole process. Compare the defaults with the team's conventions, correct the marks, set the rules, run the check, and triage every result. Clear it to zero where the language allows, and document what's left in a Project Note where it doesn't. You've seen it, now build it. Open Lesson 1 and work through the four hands-on lessons on the practice projects at your own pace. Each one has discovery prompts and an answer key to check yourself against. Then take on the scenario bank. When you've configured all three languages, send your configurations and answers to your mentor for review. See you in Paratext."

docs.title: Notes for the presenter
docs.text:
• This is an orientation, not a tutorial. Resist the urge to complete every exercise on camera. The lessons are where learners do the clicking; the video's job is to make the tool and the workflow familiar so they aren't lost when they start. If any segment runs long, cut demo depth, not the concept framing.
  • Recording order and project state. Every practice project arrives at Paratext 9.5's default Quotation Rules. Record the cold open, the Segment 1 Quote marks tab pan, and the first two rows of Segment 2 on a freshly received, unchanged TAMBA, before making any of the Lesson 2 changes. The RUNDA (1110) and MENDA ("No errors found") cuts in Segment 1 also need those projects unchanged. The Segment 2 "No errors found" run on TAMBA, and the corrected Runda and Menda tabs, come only after following Exercise 2.1 (and Exercise 2.2 / Scenario B) exactly. Segment 4 uses TAMBAB, not TAMBA.
  • Never imply the text is wrong in the cold open. The five John 17 results come from the default settings, and Tamba's text there is correct. Don't add, delete or retype any mark in the text on camera to make a result go away, and don't open the John 17 verses or describe their content. The point is what the tool is reading, not the language.
  • Say "Paratext's defaults", not "the team's settings". The defaults are what every new project gets. Never describe them as a choice the translation team made, or as a "configured" project.
  • Per-lesson clips. If a full click-by-click walkthrough of a lesson is wanted later, record it as a separate short clip per lesson rather than bloating this overview past ~15 minutes.
  • Terms to show on screen (not just say): define real error vs. configuration problem with the Segment 4 slide, and put the Unicode code points (U+201C, U+2019, U+00AB, U+203A, U+2039, U+2014) on screen wherever you name a character — the visual glyphs are easy to confuse and the code point is the ground truth.
  • Live-demo caution: always drive character entry with the dropdown (▼), never the keyboard, on camera — it models the habit the course insists on and avoids accidentally entering a straight quote. The one thing that is typed is the Continuer required at list; type it exactly as given, with single spaces.
  • Fresh runs only. To show a changed result, close the results panel and run the check again from Run basic checks. Rerun on an open panel keeps showing the old results.
  • Pronunciation / naming: Tamba, Runda, Velna, Menda and Waku are course names for practice projects built from real languages' text; say them plainly. Don't name, describe or make claims about the real languages behind them, and don't read any of the text aloud.
  • Screen legibility: the yellow information bar (Segment 1), the five John 17 result rows (cold open), the Example preview and the Continuer required at field (Segment 2), and the reversed guillemets (Segment 5) are small UI details — zoom or crop the recording so they read clearly at video resolution.
  • Do not present the recommended-settings values as authoritative. Say "your Paratext build shows the recommended defaults" rather than reading a fixed table — the exact defaults should be confirmed against the learner's actual 9.5 build.
  • Gaps flagged (not filled here): this script assumes the screenshots ss-*.png in the module folder reflect current Paratext 9.5 UI. If the recording reveals the UI has drifted, flag it to the lesson author rather than re-editing lesson content from the recording.
